newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SACKED HUNGARY MINISTER DENIES LIABLILITY IN SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: SACKED HUNGARY MINISTER DENIES LIABLILITY IN SCANDAL.

text.p: Sacked Hungarian Industry and Trade Minister Tamas Suchman on Thursday denied any legal responsibility for the scandal which has engulfed the country's privatisation agency APV and led to his dismissal.

Suchman was speaking publicly for the first time about the case in which a consultant Marta Tocsik was paid a "success fee" of 804 million forints ($5.2 million) for negotiating compensation deals for APV with local authorities for land on which privatised state companies were located.

"In the Tocsik affair I have no legal responsibility, I gave no orders, I did not tolerate the affair, I do not know the lady and I don't have the money," Suchman told Hungarian news agency MTI after appearing before Parliament's Constitutional Committee which is investigating the affair.

Hungary's Chief Prosecutor said on Tuesday he had ordered an investigation of the activities of Tocsik and other unnamed APV officials and on Wednesday the Constitutional Committee began its own inquiry at which Tocsik failed to appear.

Suchman told the Constitutional Committee on Thursday that total claims of local councils against APV amounted to 40-80 billion forints while the 1996 central budget has allocated HUF 15bn to the APV this year to satisfy the claims.

Suchman said he accepted political responsibility for the affair but maintained there was no corruption at APV and the inquiry concerned only Marta Tocsik"s unlawful legal practices and the exorbitant fee she had received for her services.

Asked by the committee whether the government was aware of the bargain with local councils and if so why it did not take a decision on the matter, Suchman said the cabinet and the Prime Minister Horn were aware of the negotiations, but that there was no need for the government to intervene.
Suchman was dismissed last Sunday by the Prime Minister Horn and will remain in office until October 15.
